claim: a constructively certified arrival time is achievable on a real lane network
result: REFUTED on this route. Seven arrivals, seven LATE, none early. Single vehicle +0.956 to +4.678 s; three vehicles +5.238 to +9.678 s. Tolerance 0.1 s declared before the run.
mechanism: SUMO safety layer overrode the commanded speed on 52-144 of ~780-1550 steps (single) and up to 652 (three). The network has 4 traffic lights against 378 unregulated priority junctions, so this is junction right-of-way logic, not signals, and no route avoids it.
consequence: Rule A admits SUPPORTED only when every arrival set UNDER-approximates. A witness arriving 4.7 s late is not UNDER on the network. On a real network, under the construction as it stands, NO OPPORTUNITY CAN BE SUPPORTED - the same conclusion previously reached for predictive models, now for constructive ones.
limits: one route, one TRAINING map, seven measurements; a consistent direction with an identified mechanism, not a proof; replication required
not_done: no delay margin was fitted to the seven measurements; that would convert a refutation into a calibration
